Cadence check. The saved feature-engineering run contains hourly MW rows; the written forecasting contract describes quarter-hour rows (23/24/25 versus 92/96/100 Berlin-local rows per day). Confirm the intended cadence before reusing a window or a reported score.

The Feature table is the overview. The Correlation map shows which columns move together in a stated sample; use forward validation to establish added predictive value.

What belongs in each Atlas section?

Feature table: forecast-time candidate columns, plain-language purpose, formula and executable recipe. Variables & targets: raw measurements, derived observed quantities, and realized outcome labels. Models & tuning: proposed or saved model settings, declared features and experiment evidence. Correlation map: descriptive coefficients and pair counts among observed variables or candidate feature columns in a stated sample. Team guide: separate contribution paths and a copyable request for Claude.

Guided discovery

Start with a question

Curated starting points for exploration, not a learned or predictive feature ranking.

Recipe setup · local install and your CSV input

Extract the ZIP, open a terminal in the package root, and install its local package and dependencies with python -m pip install -e .. The ZIP contains no source CSV. Point the Python setup at your own file. Rename fields and convert units if your schema differs. Required fields: timestamp_utc, Grid Load, Wind Onshore, Wind Offshore, Solar. Optional audit fields: Residual Load (SMARD) and available_at_utc. Timestamps must be UTC aware and grid values declared average MW. The normalizer accepts aligned 15 or 60 minute cadence; inspect gaps and the returned availability audit.

The example selects the last 24 observed UTC timestamps for a retrospective calculation. Define a separate target schedule for prospective use. Stress and regime recipes fit frozen pre-2021 calibration explicitly; source vintages require independent verification.

Experiment receipts

Models & tuning

Select a model to inspect its declared settings. Keep feature recipe settings, source-availability assumptions, model hyperparameters, and evaluation choices distinct. A fixed setting is not an optimized setting.

Have a new model idea? Open the team model guide →

Tuning protocol for a future experiment

1 · Define the taskFreeze target, issue time, horizons, decision metric, and authorized feature versions.
2 · Search within training timeFit preprocessing and choose parameters on chronological inner folds only.
3 · Preserve a receiptLog trial settings, code and data vintages, per-fold metrics, tail support, and cost.
4 · Compare against baselineEvaluate once on untouched outer folds, including relevant regimes and error tails.
No optimum is implied. Unless a source-backed experiment explicitly records a search and its results, parameters shown here are fixed experimental settings.

Associations in the current view

A keyboard-accessible sample of the largest absolute measured correlations; sorting is descriptive, not a feature ranking.

Interpretation. Pairwise correlation is symmetric association, not predictive importance, conditional value, causation, or evidence that a column was available at forecast issue. Interpret method, support, source vintage, and temporal splits before using a feature.

Team workflow

Extend the Feature Atlas

Choose what you want to add: a source measurement, a derived observed quantity, a target / label, a forecast-time feature, or a proposed model. This page is a read-only generated snapshot; these links open instructions and do not edit files, recalculate correlations, or train models.

Add source variable →Add derived observed variable →Add target / label →Add forecast feature →Add model →

Want Claude to implement an addition? Open the copyable Claude request →

PR #29 contains only static docs/ files, not the Python generator or its JSON catalogs. Work from the separate source bundle, then offer the rebuilt files and reviewed source changes in a follow-up PR. A file:// link works only on the computer holding the file; a hosted link can be shared after the repository owner chooses to publish it.

01 · Ingest a measurement

Add a source variable

  1. Document the provider, original column, physical unit, interval meaning, UTC event timestamp, cadence, missing values, and historical available_at_utc or publication delay. Establish whether the value is a measurement or a forecast issued at a recorded time.
  2. Extend and validate the fixed SMARD input mapping in feature_supermarket/recipes.py (normalize_smard_mw) to accept and normalize the new column; inspect units before combining it with average-MW series. Add its source definition to catalog/evidence.json under primitive_observed_variables and add a meaningful ingestion check.
  3. If the variable belongs in the observed-variable heatmap, calculate its descriptive correlations and pair counts from a documented common dataset, then update catalog/observed_variables_matrix.json with its source and method. The existing scripts/refresh_atlas.py does not rebuild this observed-variable matrix. To use the variable for forecasting, add a separate origin-eligible feature recipe and test its availability.

02 · Define an observed calculation

Add a derived observed variable

  1. Write the formula using named parent measurements, including units, zero-denominator and missing-value behavior, timestamp alignment, and whether it produces a target/outcome or an historical observation. For example, historical wind plus solar is the sum of three aligned MW measurements.
  2. Compute and validate the quantity in the source transformations (for the existing SMARD schema, feature_supermarket/recipes.py) and describe it in catalog/evidence.json under derived_observed_variables or target_only_outcomes, as appropriate. A target-time outcome must not be used as a future predictor.
  3. Recalculate and review catalog/observed_variables_matrix.json separately if this variable should appear on that heatmap. Updating the data dictionary alone does not generate a column or refresh the observed-variable matrix; scripts/refresh_atlas.py currently rebuilds only candidate-feature correlations.

03 · Define the outcome

Add a target / label

  1. Declare the prediction question, UTC target interval, outcome formula, class or physical unit, and which realized source values define it. Keep the existing names stress_high, stress_low, and stress_negative unchanged: they mean residual_load_mw > frozen pre-2021 P95, residual_load_mw < frozen pre-2021 P05, and residual_load_mw < 0, respectively. A new outcome needs its own distinct name and definition.
  2. Implement and validate its calculation using realized target-interval observations, joining by target_time_utc; register the definition in catalog/evidence.json under target_only_outcomes. If a label needs a percentile or other fitted threshold, fit or freeze it on an eligible earlier reference or training window, save its units and provenance, and never refit on validation or future outcomes.
  3. Keep target / label columns out of forecast predictors and the candidate-feature correlation matrix. Update the target used by relevant models and evaluation separately; gridstress_features/model_registry.py currently permits only residual_load_mw regression and stress_any classification in team model proposals, so a new label also needs an explicitly reviewed registry and model-pipeline extension. Report class prevalence, missing labels, and forward-fold scores under the new definition. The current Atlas refresh does not calculate a new target, rescore models, or refresh target-specific evidence. Changing a label definition means earlier scores describe a different task.

04 · Forecast-time recipe + definition

Add a forecast feature

  1. For a feature derived from existing registered feature columns, write a reviewed numeric pandas.Series function in gridstress_features/team_recipes.py and register its stable ID in TEAM_FEATURE_RECIPES. The function receives only declared parent feature columns. If you need a new raw input, first add its source variable and extend the feature builder rather than claiming the current parent-only extension can ingest it.
  2. Add a card with the same ID to catalog/team_features.json: explanation, formula, family, known parents, units, parameters, forecast origin, source availability, question, executable call, and evidence status. New cards must start PROPOSED_UNSCORED. Edit catalog/questions.json separately if it should appear in the curated question suggestions.
  3. Run tests and refresh against your own compatible CSV spanning the whole requested UTC year. The refresh validates registered team features, rebuilds the candidate Pearson and Spearman matrices, and generates HTML and notebook snapshots. Inspect missingness, pairwise support, forecast-time availability, and source hash before proposing the new snapshot.
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python scripts/refresh_atlas.py --csv /path/to/smard_hourly.csv --year 2024

Run these commands from the extracted source bundle root; choose the year actually covered by your CSV. The observed-variable matrix is a separate saved artifact and is not recomputed by this command.

05 · Model receipt

Add a model

  1. Add a uniquely named receipt to catalog/team_models.json with task, algorithm, intended feature bundle, data and timing contract, fixed hyperparameters, proposed tuning search space, and provenance. Label new models PROPOSED_UNSCORED.
  2. Run the tests and refresh command above. The generated Models tab reads validated model receipts automatically; refresh does not fit a model, tune settings, or create a performance score.
  3. Run training and parameter search as a separate, recorded experiment with chronological inner and untouched outer folds. Attach real metrics and source vintages only after that experiment has been reviewed.
Ask Claude to help add or update a PowerNap item

Open the editable Atlas source bundle and the separate grid-stress Git checkout in Claude Code. The current PR contains only generated HTML and a README; Claude needs the source bundle to create or rebuild a feature. Supply the new item's name, inputs, units, timestamps, availability, and a qualified data path when calculations are requested.

Where Claude should work: source measurements and observed calculations → feature_supermarket/recipes.py plus catalog/evidence.json; target labels → catalog/evidence.json and reviewed outcome/evaluation code; forecast features with existing parents → gridstress_features/team_recipes.py plus catalog/team_features.json; models → catalog/team_models.json; wording and navigation → web/index.html. Observed-variable correlations, question suggestions, target scores and model training each need their own review.

If clipboard access fails, the request stays selected above; press ⌘C on Mac or Ctrl+C elsewhere. Review Claude’s code, data assumptions and source diff before publishing a new snapshot.

Where changes are saved. Reviewed Python code and JSON manifests live in the separate source bundle. Candidate-feature correlation outputs live in catalog/feature_correlations.json; the observed-variable matrix lives in catalog/observed_variables_matrix.json and needs its own recalculation. The refresh writes HTML and notebook snapshots to dist/. Your CSV remains at the path you provided and is not embedded in the published page. Publish updated snapshots only after review and the repository owner's decision.
